messages:
taylor-sre: Heads up — got a report that analytics pipeline read a customer blob it shouldn't have after yesterday's RBAC refactor. KMS decrypts show successful decrypts for svc-analytics@prod but CloudTrail has no corresponding KMS Decrypt events. anyone seeing this? cc @olivia-sec @mike-iam

olivia-sec: on it, pulling key policy + recent IAM changes. can you paste the pipeline log snippet?

mike-iam: checking role-mappings and token cache invalidation. we recently changed role->principal glue in the refactor. cache TTL was 30m, maybe old bindings stuck.

james-prodops: saw alert from our data-loss monitor at 03:45 UTC. quick grep shows service account made a call that returned plaintext S3 object after decrypt. logs:```
2026-11-17T03:44:58Z svc=svc-analytics action=decrypt result=SUCCESS key=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:1111:key/abcd-1234 principal=svc-analytics@prod request_id=req-9fa2
```

olivia-sec: hmm. CloudTrail KMS Data Events are enabled but I don't see a matching Decrypt entry for that request_id in the KMS logs. either CloudTrail dropped the event or the decrypt came via a different auth path that bypasses KMS audit (key policy principal?).

mike-iam: I pulled the key policy diff from the deploy at 03:12 UTC — looks like during the refactor we added a permissive principal entry to the key policy to make tests easier: "Principal": "*" for the analytics-key in the temp patch. that would allow direct decrypts without IAM enforcement in some cases.

maria-eng: confirm — I deployed a quick hotfix yesterday that added a temp policy to unblock testing, forgot to remove before the refactor merged. bad on me.

security-oncall: ok first steps: 1) detach the offending principal/role from prod immediately 2) rotate any short-lived credentials if possible 3) add emergency deny on the key via a condition if we can 4) preserve forensic evidence (don't revoke logs)

mike-iam: detaching role from svc-analytics now. running: `aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name svc-analytics-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::1111:policy/analytics-temp`

deploy-bot: rollback trigger requested by maria-eng — rollback of commit 7f3c2 to pre-refactor state started. CI/CD: canary rollback in progress.

incident-bot: created SEC-2026-874: "analytics KMS decrypt exposure" and linked runbook.

olivia-sec: audit note: because key policy allowed wildcard, decrypts appear as key-owner actions and didn't generate expected IAM principal mapping in CloudTrail. we need to avoid wildcard principals in key policies. Forensics: snapshot KMS Key policy history, CloudTrail logs, and the pipeline host logs.

james-prodops: after detaching role and rollback, I'm seeing decrypt calls drop to zero from svc-analytics. monitoring metrics: decrypt_count(svc-analytics) -> 0 over last 4m.

maria-eng: apologies — follow-up actions from my side: 1) PR to remove wildcard from key policy + enforce reviewer check 2) add automated lint that rejects changes to KMS key policy without sec approval 3) run a scan for any other key policies that temporarily had permissive principals

mike-iam: additional mitigation: rotating the key would be disruptive. instead we'll add an explicit Deny for `arn:aws:iam::1111:role/svc-analytics-role` in a service control policy scoped to prod until we can patch key policy safely.

security-oncall: agree. also enable KMS CloudTrail verbose logging and compare request_ids against S3 access logs. schedule a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow 1500 UTC.

olivia-sec: monitoring in place. no more unexpected decrypts in past 8m. I'll assemble a short remediation doc and proposed gating for key policy changes.

maria-eng: will open PR for the remediation doc and the lint rule now. thanks for the quick triage everyone. :thumbsup:
